statement: Show that $x-1$ is a factor of $x^{3}-6x^{2}+11x-6$, and hence factorise the cubic completely. Deduce the three roots of $x^{3}-6x^{2}+11x-6=0$.
solution: Let $f(x)=x^{3}-6x^{2}+11x-6$. Then $f(1)=1-6+11-6=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor. Dividing, $f(x)=(x-1)(x^{2}-5x+6)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$. Hence the roots are $x=1,2,3$.
hints: Divide by (x-1) to get a quadratic.
Factorise the quadratic and read off the roots.
